supports: (13) Compensatory storage must be provided when fill is used for development within the special flood hazard area or supplemental flood zone with the exception to major highways and publicly owned facilities. ... reviewNotes: Existing carolina-forest-sc.json folds Forestbrook into its copy. Before publishing, remove foldedFrom forestbrook-sc and replace that Forestbrook block with a short link to this page.
No local association's turf approval policy verified. Similar names in TX/FL were rejected; no fees, deadlines, contact or approval policy asserted.
Prior research's claimed July 2025 Census population estimate is unsupported: current QuickFacts marks that estimate not applicable. No demographics retained.
Do not inherit aggregate recipes, universal no-permit statements or flood-prevention promises.
Phase 4 mappings follow retained customer-facing statements. Original observations and checked dates are preserved; this edit is not a new source verification.

2026-09-13: folded in Socastee (unincorporated Horry County). Its Ch. 9 compensatory-storage rule is the same one already covered on this page for Forestbrook; Sec. 9-51(13) quote reused from the Grand Strand pet-turf evidence record, itself pulled from the Municode API (Sec. 9-33's rendered page returned only its JS shell to curl/WebFetch). Socastee Historic District (National Register) carries no independent local rule found. The Socastee Overlay Zone (Sec. 807) could not be opened by any allowed method (horrycounty-sc.elaws.us timed out, Municode returned 403) and is not cited on the page.
